Subject: SIG request — audit logs & admin activity evidence

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SIG assessment we need a clear description and sample evidence for Redwood's admin activity and audit logging. Specifically we need:
- A list of event types you log (admin console actions, API calls, auth events, model deploys, inference events, key rotations, role/permission changes).
- Default retention windows for hosted / dedicated / private deployments and whether retention is configurable per account.
- Export options: scheduled snapshots, on-demand bundles, streaming to SIEM (syslog / Kinesis / Event Hubs), file formats, and whether manifests are signed.
- Chain-of-custody and tamper-evidence (hashes, signed manifests, timestamps).
- Any PII redaction or masking steps performed on export.

If you can provide a short example export or manifest (not full logs), and a playbook we can attach to the SIG submission, that would be ideal.

We have a target deadline of Apr 18 for initial packet.

Regards,
Alice Jensen
Security Analyst, Acme Health
security@acmehealth.com

From: naomi.feldman@redwood.com

Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 9 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG request — audit logs & admin activity evidence

Hi Alice / Acme security team,

Thanks — happy to put this together. High level answers below; attaching a short schema CSV and a one-page export playbook for your packet (redwood_log_schema_v2.csv, audit_export_playbook_v1.pdf).

1) What we log (examples):
- Authentication events: successful/failed logins, 2FA events, SSO assertions, IP and user agent.
- Authorization & IAM changes: role assignments, policy updates, service-account key creation/rotation/deletion.
- Admin console actions: user invites/removals, permission changes, configuration updates.
- API & management plane calls: model deployment, rollback, scaling events, configuration changes.
- Inference & routing metadata (control-plane): request id, model id, route used, token counts, latency metrics (we do NOT store full prompt/response payloads in audit logs by default for hosted customers).
- Billing/usage events: reservations, quota changes, plan changes.
- Operator activity (for Dedicated/Private): host-level operations and agent actions.

2) Default retention and configurability: 
- Hosted (default): operational audit logs retained 90 days; can be extended to 1 year for compliance add-on. Exports for SOC/SIG requests available on-demand.
- Dedicated: default 1 year; customer can choose longer retention via reserved-account policy (up to 7 years) — typically retained inside the customer-dedicated S3/GCS bucket.
- Private / On-prem: retention is controlled by customer's storage and retention policies; Redwood provides export tooling and guidance.

3) Export options & formats:
- Scheduled snapshots: daily NDJSON/CSV snapshots delivered to a customer S3/GCS path (s3://..., gs://...).
- On-demand evidence bundle: ad-hoc ZIP with NDJSON files, a machine-readable manifest (JSON) listing files, SHA256 hashes, and a human-readable summary PDF.
- Streaming: optional real-time forwarding to customer SIEM via syslog/TCP, Kinesis, Event Hubs, or a secure webhook.
- Formats: NDJSON preferred for event-driven ingestion; CSV available for small exports. Timestamps are ISO8601 (UTC).
- Signed manifests: exports include a SHA256 manifest and an optional Redwood-signed manifest (PKCS7) for tamper-evidence if requested.

4) Chain-of-custody & tamper-evidence:
- Each export bundle includes: (a) a manifest listing file names, counts, and SHA256 hashes, (b) UTC timestamped generation time, (c) Redwood service principal signature (if requested), (d) delivery logs (which S3 path / URL and the user who requested).
- For Hosted evidence deliveries we can provide a signed manifest and a short audit trail trace (who requested the export, IP address, and request-id).
- For Dedicated/Private, customers typically retain evidence in their own object storage (we provide the manifest).

5) PII redaction & payload handling:
- Audit logs are scoped to metadata; by default we avoid storing full prompt/response text in audit logs.
- If a customer enables extended tracing for debugging we store request/response with redaction tools available; exports can be configured to mask or hash specific fields.
- We can apply field-level redaction rules during export (email/hash or redact) per customer policy.

Next steps: Monica (cc'd) will prepare a short sample export bundle (manifest + brief sample NDJSON events) and Rishi can confirm signed-manifest workflow. Can you confirm the delivery channel you prefer (S3 path we can write to, or secure Drive link for initial review)?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Security Program Manager | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

Naomi — this is great, thanks. Quick follow-ups so we can slot the materials into the SIG spreadsheet:

If possible we'd like the sample bundle in the Drive link you provided. Also include a tiny sample showing an auth event and an admin role-change event in NDJSON.

From: naomi.feldman@redwood.com

Hi Alice — quick replies inline and I've uploaded the sample bundle to the Drive folder (link above). Attachments in the Drive: sample_auth_event.ndjson, sample_admin_change.ndjson, sample_manifest.json, export_readme.txt.

- Retention configurability (hosted): 90-day default can be extended via the Console for customers on the compliance add-on. For legacy accounts we can change retention on request; for new accounts the Console toggle is available under Settings > Data Retention.

- Manifest & signature: the manifest contains a SHA256 hash per file. We sign the manifest with Redwood's export key (PKCS7). Verification steps (brief): 1) download the manifest and the signature file; 2) fetch the Redwood public cert from https://public-keys.redwood.com/export-key.pem; 3) run: openssl smime -verify -in manifest.sig -inform DER -content manifest.json -certfile export-key.pem -noverify; 4) confirm SHA256 hashes match the files. I'll include a short verification snippet in the Drive README.

- Un-redacted internal copies: we do not retain un-redacted customer payloads for Hosted customers beyond a short debug window (30 days) unless the customer explicitly enables extended tracing. For Dedicated/Private, un-redacted traces are stored only in customer-controlled storage. If extended tracing is enabled, retention and access controls are documented and agreed in the SOC/SLA.

Action items: 
- Monica: produce the sample NDJSON + manifest and upload to shared Drive (cc'd).
- Rishi: please confirm whether we should include the PKCS7 signature by default for Hosted evidence deliveries or keep it an opt-in per customer.
- Stephanie: flag any SOC2/SIG language we should add to the export_readme to ease review.

Alice — if you confirm Drive delivery is fine for the packet I'll mark this as ready for your Apr 18 cut.

Thanks all,
Naomi
